results.title: Design and evaluation of psychometric properties of cigarette smoking tendency questionnaire for female adolescents (CTQFA) | BMC Public Health | Full Text
results.content: Design and evaluation of psychometric properties of cigarette smoking tendency questionnaire for female adolescents (CTQFA) # Design and evaluation of psychometric properties of cigarette smoking tendency questionnaire for female adolescents (CTQFA) *BMC Public Health* **volume 21**, Article number: 1746 (2021) Cite this article ## Abstract ### Background The tendency of women to smoke has increased in recent years and the prevalence of smoking among women is increasing. ### Conclusion Based on the results of this questionnaire, 52 questions, and 5 subscales can be used to assess the tendency of female adolescents to cigarette smoking. ### Reliability Based on the results of Cronbach’s alpha coefficients for 5 subscales of tendency to experience smoking, re-experience smoking, cigarette dependence, intention to quit smoking, and smoking cessation were 0.840, 0.844, 0.890, 0.849, and 0.867, respectively. Based on the Barati’s study, the results of the CFA showed that the belief-based tobacco smoking scale with 34-item and 4 subscales had an acceptable construct validity (RMSEA = 0.057; CFI = 0.933; IFI = 0.934; TLI = 0.918; GFI = 0.908 > 0.9). Based on the results of the Sterling study, the questionnaire of scales of smoking related self-efficacy, beliefs, and intention had acceptable construct validity (CFI = 0.96, NNFI = 0.96, RMSEA = 0.08) [28:310–5. Based on the Blake’s study, the psychometric results of the smoking restraint questionnaire showed that the goodness of fit indices of the model had standard values (RMSEA =0.038, CFI = 0.99, TLI = 0.99) and the construct validity of the questionnaire was verified [31:238–45. Based on the psychometric results of the adolescent reasons for quitting smoking scale questionnaire, the 55 questions questionnaire in the CFA section explained 55% of the variance and had acceptable construct validity. The results of this study showed that the questionnaire of the tendency of female adolescents to cigarette smoking can be used as a valid tool to assess the current situation and evaluate programs related to smoking prevention in girls. Article  PubMed  PubMed Central  Google Scholar Cigarette smoking as a risk factor for coronary heart disease in women compared with men: a systematic review and meta-analysis of prospective cohort studies. *et al.* Design and evaluation of psychometric properties of cigarette smoking tendency questionnaire for female adolescents (CTQFA).

results.title: Cutoff criteria: Significance and symbolism
results.content: # Significance of Cutoff criteria. Cutoff criteria are standard thresholds used in statistical modeling. Health Sciences utilizes these criteria to assess a model's fit and reliability. They act as benchmarks, helping researchers determine if a model accurately represents the data and produces consistent results. By applying these criteria, researchers can evaluate the performance of their models and make informed decisions about their validity. Synonyms: Parameters, Requirements, Threshold, Limit, Boundary, Exclusion criteria, Elimination criteria, Selection criteria. The below excerpts are indicatory and do represent direct quotations or translations. It is your responsibility to fact check each reference. ## The concept of Cutoff criteria in scientific sources. Cutoff criteria, in statistical modeling, involves standard thresholds. These thresholds are essential for assessing a model's accuracy and dependability. They help determine how well the model fits the data and ensures reliable results. (1) These are standards used to assess fit, analyzed with alternatives. (2) These are specific values used as thresholds to determine whether a statistical result is considered significant or meaningful. (3) The overall fit indices met the cutoff criteria, which are the established thresholds for determining whether a model provides an adequate fit to the data, with values such as RMSEA (< 0.08), SRMR (< 0.08), NNFI (> 0.95), and CFI (> 0.95) indicating acceptable fit. From: *International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health (MDPI)*. (1) The text refers to "cutoff criteria", which are standards used for assessing fit indexes within covariance structure analysis, contrasting conventional criteria with newer alternatives. (2) They are used for fit indexes in covariance structure analysis, indicating a statistical method for assessing the fit of a model to the data. From: *The Malaysian Journal of Medical Sciences*. (1) These are standards used to determine acceptability in statistical analyses. (2) Standard thresholds used in statistical modeling to evaluate the fit and reliability of a model.
